The server listens on `127.0.0.1`\nusing the port given by the `PORT` environment variable (default `3000`).\n\nQuick health check:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:3000/health\n```\n\nExpected response:\n\n```json\n{ \"ok\": true }\n```\n\nReset the SQLite database during testing:\n\n```bash\ncurl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/storage/reset\n```\n\n## Entry point and major modules\n\n| File / directory | Responsibility |\n| --- | --- |\n| `src/server.ts` | Entry point. Creates the `node:http` server, parses JSON bodies, dispatches requests to the router, and listens on `127.0.0.1`. |\n| `src/router.ts` | Central route table. Matches the request method and path, extracts path parameters, and delegates to the appropriate route handler. |\n| `src/routes/*.ts` | One route module per API domain. Each exports small, synchronous handler functions that write JSON responses. |\n| `src/db.ts` | SQLite connection singleton, schema definition, schema version, and `resetDatabase()`. |\n| `src/repository.ts` | All SQL reads and writes. If it matches, the response is sent and the\n   request is done.\n3. If the method is not `POST` and not a known GET route, `405 Method Not\n   Allowed` is returned.\n4.
